title: Gatekeeper economic rules for cheap variants
summary: Compact working proposal for a lightweight gatekeeper that ties quality checks to lower-cost model/config variants. Focus is on pragmatic thresholds, quick signal engineering from existing evals, and a rollout checklist that minimizes eval spend while protecting user-facing quality.
body:
Context and motivation:
Most teams want to try cheaper model configurations (quantized weights, reduced context, small wrappers) but avoid user-visible regressions. We need a crisp, low-overhead gate system that sits between the cost-savings recommendations produced by Optimize and rollout mechanisms (canary / fallback). This doc sketches: minimal signals to catch regressions, cost-vs-quality heuristics, spreadsheet example rows, and an operational checklist for experiments and rollouts.

Design goals (non-exhaustive):
- Lightweight: rely on small eval subsets + fast automation, not full-scale human labeling for every change.
- Conservative by default: cheaper variants must prove parity on primary signals before hitting production routes.
- Incremental: support staged opening of cheaper paths (A/B -> partial -> full) with automatic rollback triggers.
- Measurable economics: show expected tokens saved per 100k requests and a projected $ savings per month in the spreadsheet.

Signals to compute (fast, automatable):
- Topline metric: Delta-accept-rate (DAR): fraction of prompts where cheaper variant output passes automated accept filters (e.g., exact-match for deterministic tasks, embedding distance threshold for semantic tasks).
- Soft-regression: Embedding drift (cosine) relative to baseline with task-specific threshold.
- Behavior safeties: number of policy-triggered tokens flagged by existing prod safety classifier per 10k responses.
- Latency tail: p95 delta; regressions here are often UX-visible.
- Cost delta: tokens/unit * price-per-token variant = per-response $ change; normalized per 100k.

Threshold heuristics (working defaults — tune per-customer):
- DAR >= 98% for high-sensitivity tasks (billing, legal), >= 95% for general assistants, >= 90% for low-risk retrieval/embeddings.
- Embedding cosine >= 0.92 for embeddings-critical flows, >= 0.88 for semantic similarity fallbacks.
- Safety flags: no more than 0.5x baseline increase; any >2x triggers immediate rollback.
- Latency p95 improvement of at least 10ms for batch-based savings to be worth complexity; otherwise prefer caching.

Spreadsheet example (row format described so product can plug into Optimize spreadsheet):
- id: gate-2026-03-10-001
- variant: 4-bit-quantized-gpt-small-cache-on
- baseline_model: gpt-medium-32k
- task_category: customer-support-summary
- eval_subset_size: 1500 prompts (stratified by intent and length)
- DAR: 96.7%
- embed_cos: 0.90
- safety_ratio: 1.1x
- p95_latency_ms_delta: -42
- est_tokens_saved_per_100k: 1.4M
- est_monthly_savings_usd: $1,900
- gate_status: conditional-pilot

Evaluation plan (fast path vs thorough path):
- Fast path (recommended for initial experiments): use 200–2,000 stratified prompts + automated comparators (exact-match, embedding distance, toxicity heuristics). Run nightly until stable for 3 consecutive days. Low human overhead.
- Thorough path (for staged rollout to major customers): expand to 10k prompts, include human blind-labeling sample (n=500) for nuanced quality checks and a subjective satisfaction panel.

Decision matrix (how Optimize should decide next action):
- If DAR >= threshold AND embed_cos >= threshold AND safety_ratio <= baseline*1.5 -> mark as pilot eligible (10% traffic).
- If pilot results (7 days) maintain thresholds -> escalate to 50% traffic with continued monitoring.
- Any safety_ratio >2x or DAR drop >5 percentage points in pilot -> automatic immediate rollback and tag variant as ‘blocked’; require human review.

Budget/Cost control knobs:
- Per-variant eval budget cap: default $750 for fast path evaluations, $5k for thorough path. Limits configurable per-customer.
- Auto-abort if accumulated eval spend exceeds projected monthly savings for the variant. (Prevent chasing diminishing returns.)

Operational checklist (pre-pilot):
- Confirm stratified eval set completed and stored (drive id in linked_artifacts).
- Attach model artifact id and quantization recipe to the gate row.
- Run 3x nightly automated runs; check for flakiness (variance >1.5% DAR).
- Verify tracing hooks and per-token cost tags are enabled in the console route.
- Define rollback owner and on-call for first 72 hours.

Rollout and monitoring alerts (quick list):
- Alert A (severity high): safety_ratio >2x baseline -> immediate rollback.
- Alert B (severity medium): DAR drop >3 percentage points week-over-week -> reduce traffic to variant by half and notify product.
- Alert C (info): p95 latency regression >50ms -> investigate kernel selection / batch strategy.

Example real-world scenario (compact):
- Customer: eComm search (high volume, low-risk content). Baseline: 3B float model. Variant: 3B q4 with prefix cache. Fast-path eval n=1k shows DAR 94.6% (tolerance 90%), embed_cos 0.91. Est monthly savings $12k. Action: pilot at 15% traffic with automatic fallback to baseline on low embed cosine for top-1 results. After 14 days, DAR stable -> escalate to 60% with safety ratio watch.

Notes on instrumentation and signal quality: 
- Embedding thresholds must be calibrated per task and per prompt-length bucket. Simple global cutoffs cause false positives. We recommend a short calibration job that computes baseline distributions and per-context-cluster thresholds before gate evaluation.
- For deterministic tasks (invoices, legal snippets), prefer exact-match and token-level diff heuristics rather than embeddings.

Open questions / tradeoffs (for discussion):
- How aggressive should auto-abort be for low-dollar variants where user impact is small but operational toil is high? (Option: higher DAR tolerance for low-revenue routes.)
- Should we include human-in-the-loop sampling for every variant that changes quantization table? (Costly but catches subtle hallucinations.)
- How to encode partial-fallback: e.g., use cheap variant for scoring and fall back to baseline for generation when confidence low — do we treat that as separate variant or an internal routing policy?

Next steps and action items (owner assigned):
- Aisha: prepare a 1-page spec for Optimize UI to surface gate rows and thresholds (due 2026-03-20).
- Liam: prototype the fast-path eval runner and example spreadsheet import/export (PR in repo by 2026-03-25).
- Marta: run calibration job for two canonical tasks (support-summary, search-retrieval) and share distributions (due 2026-03-22).
- Jun: draft alerting playbook and PagerDuty runbook snippet (due 2026-03-24).

Appendix: quick cheat-sheet for engineers (copyable):
- Quick commands: export eval set -> run_fast_eval --variant q4 --n 1000 --metrics dar,embed,safety -> upload csv to drive -> run gatekeeper-check --row-id gate-YYYYMMDD-XXX
- Minimal JSON fields for gate row ingestion: id, variant, baseline_model, task_category, eval_subset_id, dar, embed_cos, safety_ratio, p95_delta_ms, est_tokens_saved_100k, est_monthly_usd, status

Comments / notes to self:
- Keep this doc intentionally compact. Longer playbook can live in confluence (see linked artifact). This is for rapid experimenters who want practical thresholds and an example row to drop into the Optimize spreadsheet.
notes: Working draft; expect thresholds to change after calibration runs. Priority: make the fast-path safe and cheap to run so teams iterate quickly.
